correctness.rationale: A directed triangle accepts every signed word by traversing a fixed 3-cycle forwards or backwards. Every triangle-free tournament is transitive, and in a transitive k-tournament a signed path maps in exactly when its largest uniform-sign run is shorter than k, via longest incoming directed-path ranks. Any orientation of G restricts to a tournament on its k-clique, giving lower inclusion; orienting all edges by a proper k-coloring excludes every k-uniform-sign run, giving upper inclusion. The 2k-state DFA is explicitly distinguished with suffixes and the length series follows from unique maximal-run decomposition. Supplemental exact checker passed 1,099 tournaments, 760 small-graph orientations and 400 multipartite orientations.

value.rationale: A complete all-word language and minimal-DFA classification for all nonempty weakly perfect graphs, not a finite census, yields the same 2k-state canonical recognizer for arbitrarily large perfect graphs, plus a full length generating function. Mixed signed paths introduce information invisible from the pure directed-path chromatic threshold, as exhibited by C5. The result directly responds to a newly introduced graph-language invariant and delineates a natural structural boundary.
